market_question: Will the Republicans win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: The 2028 election is an open-seat race after a single Trump term, historically a coin-flip scenario. The market's 38.5% implied Republican chance seems low given how polarized and close recent elections have been (2020 and 2024 were decided by narrow margins). Even with potential party fatigue, a true probability near 45% better reflects the high uncertainty and competitive nature of US presidential contests.
evidence_points: Since 1900, parties defending an open White House after one term win roughly half the time, not 38%.
Recent elections (2016, 2020, 2024) were within a few percent, suggesting the baseline is near 50/50, not a 23-point Democratic edge.
No clear structural advantage for Democrats in the Electoral College post-2024; the tipping-point state was Pennsylvania, which Trump carried.
sources_consulted: 2024 presidential election results and electoral college analysis
General political science literature on incumbency and open‑seat races
